[b]Tuyuchi today[/b]:
The tuyuchi kingdom would have fall at the 6th century BCE, but their people remained until at as far as the 1st century After Christ , however, there is still a community which is dated from as far as the 2nd century BCE which rather migrating to the west, migrated far into the southern valleys and then around the 1st or 5th century After Christ would migrate to the top of mountains creating Cañihuas, this community still exists today and is called Tuyuchapû, or Tuyuchi from mountains, this community has very interesting traditions which exists until today, such as:
They do not bury their dead, instead they cremate and throw them at sea...but wait, they live on mountains ...yes, they travel to the coast just to cremate their dead.
Have a full oral tradition and prefer keeping mercantile tradition as simple merchants but no much, in fact the fonts mentioning these are indirect.
Their houses are made of wood and interwoven sticks with mud which dries out quite fast and human bones.
They marry between themselves.
And are quite unknown. With just about 600 people, they live trying to remain unknown...and it is quite successful until now.
